$comment: DEMO / NON-PRODUCTION PRODUCT FIXTURE (VR3-01). Every name, value, cost, date and document here is synthetic and exists only to demonstrate Product behaviour. It is not calculation authority, a quotation or a real client record. Transcribed from the accepted VR3-00 fixture specification artifacts/VR3-00-global-design-audit/06-demo-fixtures/demo-project-fixtures.md; the counts, filenames, buildings, areas, source relations, questions, conflicts and media ids are invariants of that specification and are re-proved mechanically by src/state/__tests__/projectAnalysis.test.ts (the path this comment used to name, src/fixtures/__tests__/vr3-demo-projects.test.ts, has never existed — a stale claim corrected 2026-09-08). Prose is not stored here: every user-visible sentence is an i18n key (rule 36), resolved DE/EN from src/i18n. Numbers are decimal STRINGS, never JSON numbers, so no float ever enters the model. VR3 PORTFOLIO EXTENSION (Projects portfolio rebuild): each project now also carries a `portfolio` block — the ISO country code, postcode, street, created/last-modified/next-client-meeting timestamps and the declared portfolio area metric. The block NO LONGER declares a lifecycle status: it declares `lifecycleHold`, the explicit human state (`on_hold` / `waiting_for_feedback` / `archive`) or `null`. A project's lifecycle status is DERIVED from its own committed truth by src/state/projectLifecycle.ts, so a fresh session shows both demonstration projects as `New` and no fixture can grant itself `Ready to pitch`. The timestamps tell ONE demonstration chronology and are the only thing that orders the register under the truthful last-modified sort: Freiburg 07.09 → Leipzig 05.09 → Hamburg 03.09 → Wien 02.09 → München 31.08. Changing a timestamp only to move a card, without the event that moved it, is not permitted. Those fields are PRESENTATION identity for the Projects register; they never enter the calculation, the Option or the client output. `owner` now carries the responsible manager's full first name and surname, because the portfolio filters on a person and initials are not a person.
